text:
cheng: heads-up — after landing the int8 bring-up for falcon-quant, the eval-runner started dropping ~14% of traces during ingest. logs show parser bailing on the embeddings blob header, not the gzip or manifest.

cheng: example log:
```
ERROR ingest.worker TraceParserError: unknown embedding header magic: 0x43525432 at parse_embeddings (trace_parser.py:214)
    at IngestRunner._process (ingest_runner.py:87)
    payload: {sample_id: 'abc123', model: 'falcon-quant-v3', trace_version: 2, shard: 5}
```

sophia: hmm that magic code looks like ascii for 'CRT2' or similar. did the quantized runner change alignment/endianness? :thinking_face:

marcus: we added a new compact binary header for embeddings to save ~20% per-sample. header layout: 4byte magic, 1byte flags, 1byte dtype, 2byte reserved, then length. sounds like a version bump.

cheng: right, but the parser expects big-endian length. falcon-quant runner writes little-endian length (was trying to be consistent with the model lib). so a mismatch for some builds. failing ones are all Linux x86_64 builds on the new container image.

trace-bot: Detecting increased ingestion failures for trace_version=2 since 1965431800. Failure rate: 14%. Notified #eng-ml.

ada: temporary mitigation — we can make the parser accept either endianness based on magic byte patterns. quick patch should remove user-facing failures.

ben: +1 on parser tolerance, but we should add a CI repro. plan: add a tiny synthetic trace generator that writes both endiannesses and uploads to the staging ingest. run it in the eval-runner CI matrix on PRs that touch trace parsing or quantized code.

sophia: also we need to avoid storing ~multi-MB embeddings inline in the primary object. proposal: if embedding bytes > 1MB, write to object-store as a separate blob and keep a pointer in the trace. that will reduce retention cost and make partial downloads faster for dashboards.

cheng: agreed. for immediate triage: 1) ada to open parser-accept-endian PR, 2) add CI synthetic traces job, 3) add ingest metric for "legacy-header-detected" so we can audit how many old runners still out there, 4) create migration job to rewrite recent traces to pointer format for big-embeddings.

ada: assigning to myself. quick sketch of parser change:
```
# pseudo
magic = read(4)
if magic in (b"TRC1", b"TRC2"):
  endian = "big"
elif magic in (b"CRT1", b"CRT2"):
  endian = "little"
else:
  raise TraceParserError("unknown magic")
length = read_uint16(endian=endian)
```

marcus: + we should update the trace manifest schema to include `embedding_storage: "inline"|"blob"` and a `blob_checksum` when stored externally. dashboards will need a join to show embeddings-linked metrics.

ben: I'll add the synthetic-trace CI job. it will: generate 3 traces (big inline embedding little-endian, big inline embedding big-endian, external-blob trace) and assert ingest-status == 200 and that the manifest normalizes to the canonical schema.

sophia: one more: retention TTL rules — if embedding_storage=="blob" then apply separate TTL (90 days) and mark for cheaper tier. we'll need to update the retention-runner to respect the new marker.

cheng: thanks everyone. ada — can you include a tiny sample trace (base64) in the PR description so infra can smoke test locally? also please add a small e2e in the eval harness that verifies per-sample output roundtrip for quantized models.

ada: yep. adding sample and e2e. will post PR link here when ready. :eyes:

trace-bot: New PR opened by ada: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/482 — parser endian tolerance + synthetic-trace CI. CI queued.

marcus: once merged, let's run a backfill for the last 7 days and monitor cost/ingest-stability. if backfill shows >0.5% corruption, roll back and investigate further.

ben: noted — I'll add dashboards for "legacy-header-detected" and "embedding_blob_count".

cheng: thank you all. this explains a lot of the sporadic dashboard gaps we saw in the quality regressions run. we'll re-run the falcon-quant eval after the fix and compare embeddings similarity distribution. :shipit:
